title: European children are not strong anymore

paragraphs: A new study has revealed European children and adolescents are in worse physical shape today than at almost any point over the last 60 years.

Researchers from the University of Zaragoza analyzed physical fitness data from over 417,000 young people aged 6 to 16 across 20 European countries. The findings show a worrying long-term decline in key health indicators, including muscular strength, flexibility, and overall body composition. Upper and lower body strength have steadily dropped since the 1980s, while flexibility has experienced the steepest decline, and accelerated sharply after 2000. Additionally, researchers noted a continuous increase in body fat levels among youth.
Health experts warn that physical inactivity severely threatens future well-being, as over 75% of European adolescents fail to meet the WHO’s recommendation of 60 minutes of daily physical activity.

paragraphs: A new study shows that young people in Europe are in much worse physical shape today than in past decades.

Researchers looked at health data for more than 417,000 children and teenagers from 20 European countries. They found that overall muscle strength and flexibility dropped dramatically over the last forty years. Especially after the year 2000, children became much less flexible. At the same time, body fat levels continue to grow.

Health experts explain that good physical health in childhood helps prevent serious diseases like heart problems and diabetes later in life. But more than 75% of European teenagers don’t exercise for 60 minutes every day as recommended by the World Health Organization. Experts warn that public groups must quickly encourage young people to move more.

paragraphs: A big new study shows that children in Europe are not as strong as before.

Experts check the health of over 417,000 children in 20 countries. They find that young people have less muscle strength and less flexibility than children forty years ago. Many children also have more body fat now.

Doctors say that playing and exercising helps keep hearts and bodies healthy for the future. But more than 75% of teenagers in Europe do not move enough every day. Experts say that schools and cities must help children exercise more every day. It is the best way to stay healthy.
